If the admin has disabled the ability for users to update their name format, requests to update this field for the primary login will silently fail.

replyToAddress.description: An optional email address that is included in a 'Reply-To:' header for mail sent using this alias. If this is empty, Gmail will not generate a 'Reply-To:' header.

signature.description: An optional HTML signature that is included in messages composed with this alias in the Gmail web UI. This signature is added to new emails only.

isDefault.description: Whether this address is selected as the default 'From:' address in situations such as composing a new message or sending a vacation auto-reply. Every Gmail account has exactly one default send-as address, so the only legal value that clients may write to this field is true. Changing this from false to true for an address will result in this field becoming false for the other previous default address.

treatAsAlias.description: Whether Gmail should treat this address as an alias for the user's primary email address. This setting only applies to custom 'from' aliases.

smtpMsa.description: An optional SMTP service that will be used as an outbound relay for mail sent using this alias. If this is empty, outbound mail will be sent directly from Gmail's servers to the destination SMTP service. This setting only applies to custom 'from' aliases.

host.description: The hostname of the SMTP service. Required.

port.description: The port of the SMTP service. Required.

username.description: The username that will be used for authentication with the SMTP service. This is a write-only field that can be specified in requests to create or update SendAs settings; it is never populated in responses.

password.description: The password that will be used for authentication with the SMTP service. This is a write-only field that can be specified in requests to create or update SendAs settings; it is never populated in responses.

securityMode.description: The protocol that will be used to secure communication with the SMTP service. Required.

verificationStatus.description: Indicates whether this address has been verified for use as a send-as alias. Read-only. This setting only applies to custom 'from' aliases.

name: update_vacation_settings
description: Update vacation responder settings for the specified account. These settings correspond to the 'Vacation responder' feature in the web interface

userId.description: Specifies the userId by email address or uses me to refer to the currently authenticated user.

enableAutoReply.description: Flag that controls whether Email automatically replies to messages (required field)

responseSubject.description: Optional text to prepend to the subject line in vacation responses. Required if enableAutoReply is true and responseBodyPlainText/responseBodyHtml are not provided

responseBodyPlainText.description: Response body in plain text format. Required if enableAutoReply is true and responseSubject/responseBodyHtml are not provided

responseBodyHtml.description: Response body in HTML format. Required if enableAutoReply is true and responseSubject/responseBodyPlainText are not provided. If both responseBodyPlainText and responseBodyHtml are specified, responseBodyHtml will be used

restrictToContacts.description: Flag that determines whether responses are sent to recipients who are not in the user's list of contacts. Optional, defaults to false

restrictToDomain.description: Flag that determines whether responses are sent to recipients who are outside of the user's domain. This feature is only available for Google Workspace users. Optional, defaults to false

startTime.description: An optional start time for sending auto-replies in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2025-08-30T09:00:00Z'). When this is specified, Email will automatically reply only to messages that it receives after the start time

endTime.description: An optional end time for sending auto-replies in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2025-09-05T18:00:00Z'). When this is specified, Email will automatically reply only to messages that it receives before the end time

name: verify_send_as_alias
description: Sends a verification email to the specified send-as alias address. The verification status must be pending. This method is only available to service account clients that have been delegated domain-wide authority.

userId.description: Specifies the userId by email address or uses me to refer to the currently authenticated user.

sendAsEmail.description: The send-as alias to be verified.

name: watch_user_mailbox
description: Set up or update a push notification watch on the given user mailbox

topicName.description: A fully qualified Google Cloud Pub/Sub API topic name. Should be a valid Pub/Sub

userId.description: Specifies the userId by email address or uses me to refer to the currently authenticated user.

labelIds.description: List of labelIds to restrict notifications about

name: add_new_assignment_rule
description: Create a new assignment rule with validation. Assignment rules define how HR cases are automatically routed to teams or individuals based on skills, country, priority, etc. The rule name must be unique within the organization. Skills, users, and user groups are validated against the database.

name.description: Assignment rule name (required, 1-120 characters, unique within organization). Example: 'IT Support Rules'

based_on_skills.description: List of skill IDs that trigger this rule (optional, validated). Example: [1, 2, 3]

based_on_country.description: Country code that triggers this rule (optional). Valid values: US, GB, CA, IN, DE, FR, JP, CN, AU, BR. Example: 'US'

based_on_priority.description: Priority level that triggers this rule (optional, defaults to 'planning'). Valid values: critical, high, moderate, low, planning. Example: 'high'

active.description: Whether the rule is active (default: False). Inactive rules are not applied. Example: true

user_group.description: User group ID to assign cases to (optional, must exist in organization). Example: 5

users.description: List of user IDs to assign cases to (optional, validated). Example: [10, 11, 12]

name: add_new_escalation_rule
description: Add a new escalation rule by specifying source group (escalate_from) and target group (escalate_to). Both groups must exist in the organization. Returns the created escalation rule with escalation_rule_id, escalate_from, escalate_to, escalate_from_group_name, escalate_to_group_name, created_at timestamp, and org_id.

escalate_from.description: Source group ID (required, must exist in organization)

escalate_to.description: Target group ID (required, must exist in organization)

name: add_new_group_member
description: Add a user to a group. Validates that both group and user exist in the same organization and that the user is not already a member. Returns the created membership details.

group_id.description: ID of the group to add the user to. Example: '1', '42'

user_id.description: ID of the user to add to the group. Example: '5', '123'

name: add_new_skill
description: Add a new skill to the organization. Skill name must be unique within the organization. The 'active' field is optional and defaults to True if not provided. Returns the created skill with skill_id, name, active status, and timestamps.

name.description: Skill name (required, must be unique within organization)

active.description: Active status (optional)

name: add_new_skill_to_user
description: Assign a skill to a user by creating a user_skill record. Both skill and user must exist in the organization. Returns the created assignment with enhanced details including skill_name, user_email, user_first_name, and user_last_name.

skill.description: Skill ID to assign (required, must exist in organization)

user.description: User ID to assign skill to (required, must exist in organization)

name: add_new_topic_category
description: Create a new topic category. Validates name is unique within organization and coe_type is valid enum value. Returns created topic category with timestamps.

name.description: Topic category name (required, must be unique). Examples: 'Employee Relations', 'Compensation & Benefits', 'Talent Acquisition'

coe_type.description: COE type (required). Valid values: HRIT, Payroll, Talent Management, Total Rewards, Workforce Administration

active.description: Whether topic category is active (default: true)

name: add_new_topic_detail
description: Create a new topic detail. Validates name is unique within organization and topic_category exists if provided. Returns created topic detail with expanded topic_category relationship.

name.description: Topic detail name (required, must be unique). Examples: 'New Employee Setup', 'Health Insurance', 'Payroll Changes'

active.description: Whether topic detail is active (default: true)

topic_category.description: Topic category name (optional, must exist). Examples: 'Onboarding', 'Benefits', 'Payroll'

name: add_new_user
description: Create a new user in the HR system. Validates email uniqueness within organization, name combination uniqueness, and role validity. User is automatically assigned to the requester's organization. Returns complete user details including auto-generated ID and timestamps.

first_name.description: User's first name (1-60 characters). Only letters, spaces, hyphens (-), apostrophes ('), and periods (.) allowed. Special characters like @#$%^&*() are not allowed. Examples: 'John', 'Maria', 'José', 'Mary-Jane', 'O'Brien'

last_name.description: User's last name (1-60 characters). Only letters, spaces, hyphens (-), apostrophes ('), and periods (.) allowed. Special characters like @#$%^&*() are not allowed. Examples: 'Doe', 'Garcia', 'O'Brien', 'Van Der Berg'

email.description: User's work email address (must be valid RFC-compliant email format and unique within organization). Invalid characters like *&^%#$ in email addresses are not allowed. Examples: 'john.doe@company.com', 'user+tag@example.org'

phone.description: User's phone number (optional, max 30 characters). Examples: '+1-555-123-4567', '(555) 123-4567'

role.description: User's role in the system. Determines permissions.

active.description: Whether the user account is active. Defaults to true.

name: add_new_user_group
description: Create a new user group in the HR system. Validates name uniqueness within organization and group type validity. Group is automatically assigned to the requester's organization. Returns complete group details including auto-generated ID and timestamps. Requires groups/crud permission.

name.description: Group name (1-80 characters, must be unique within organization). Only letters, spaces, hyphens (-), apostrophes ('), and periods (.) allowed. Special characters like @#$%^&*()!~` are not permitted. Examples: 'IT Support Team', 'HR Service Desk', 'L1 Support'

type.description: Group type - determines the group's purpose and capabilities

active.description: Whether the group is active. Defaults to true.

name: avg_notifications_by_case
description:
Calculate average number of notifications per case, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns the average notifications count by cases as a float.
        Example: 2.5 (meaning on average each case has 2.5 notifications)
        
        Optional parameter:
        - case_ids: List of case IDs to filter (if not provided, calculates for all cases in organization)
        
        Note: If no cases exist, returns 0.0

case_ids.description: Optional list of case IDs to filter

name: count_case_for_assignment_group
description:
Count cases assigned to an assignment group with optional filters, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns an object where assignment_group_id is the key and the number of cases assigned to it is the count value.
        Example: {'assignment_group_id': 1, 'count': 5}
        
        Required parameter:
        - assignment_group_id: Assignment group ID
        
        Optional parameters (for filtering):
        - statuses: List of case statuses to filter. Valid statuses: draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        - priority_list: List of priorities to filter. Valid priorities: critical, high, moderate, low, planning (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        - source: Source to filter. Valid sources: self-service, phone, email, chat, walk-in, virtual-agent (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        
        All filters are applied with AND logic.

statuses.description: Optional list of case statuses to filter

priority_list.description: Optional list of priorities to filter

name: count_case_task_for_assignment_group
description:
Count case tasks assigned to an assignment group with optional status filter, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns an object where assignment_group_id is the key and the number of case tasks assigned to it is the count value.
        Example: {'assignment_group_id': 1, 'count': 3}
        
        Required parameter:
        - assignment_group_id: Assignment group ID
        
        Optional parameters (for filtering):
        - statuses: List of task statuses to filter. Valid statuses: draft, ready, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, cancelled (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        
        All filters are applied with AND logic.

statuses.description: Optional list of task statuses to filter

name: count_notifications_by_case
description:
Count notifications for cases, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns the total count of notifications.
        If case_ids are provided, counts notifications for those specific cases only.
        If case_ids are not provided, counts all notifications in the organization.
        
        Optional parameter:
        - case_ids: List of case IDs to filter (if not provided, counts all notifications)

case_ids.description: Optional list of case IDs to filter

name: count_notifications_by_status
description:
Count notifications grouped by status, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns status-wise notifications count as an object with status as key and count as value.
        Example: {'draft': 5, 'ready': 3, 'work_in_progress': 2}
        
        Optional parameter:
        - status: List of statuses to filter. If provided, only those statuses are considered for output.
          Valid statuses: draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled (lowercase, case-sensitive).
          If a status list is given, the output will only include those statuses (with count 0 if not found).
          If not provided or null, returns counts for all statuses.

status.description: Optional list of statuses to filter. Valid statuses: draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled

name: count_notifications_by_type
description:
Count notifications grouped by type, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns type-wise notification count as an object with type as key and count as value.
        Example: {'report': 5, 'update': 3, 'alert': 2}
        
        Optional parameter:
        - type: List of notification types to filter. If provided, only those types are considered for output.
          Valid types: report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other (case-sensitive, lowercase).
        
        If a type list is given, the output will only include those types (with count 0 if not found).

type.description: Optional list of notification types to filter. Valid types: report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other

name: create_checklist
description: Create a new checklist item with validation. Validates that the case task exists in the database. Returns the created checklist item with all details. Use this to add new checklist items to HR case tasks.

checklist_item_description.description: Description of the checklist item. Example: 'Submit identification documents', 'Complete training sessions'

checked.description: Whether the item is checked/completed. Defaults to false if not provided.

case_task_id.description: ID of the associated case task (must exist in database). Example: 1

name: create_hr_case_task
description: Create a new HR case task with complete validation. Validates all referenced entities (parent case, assigned user, assignment group, HR service) exist in the database and belong to the organization. Automatically generates a unique task number in format TASK-YYYYMMDD-XXXX. The task is automatically scoped to the authenticated user's organization. short_description must contain at least one non-whitespace character. Returns the created task with all relationships fully expanded.

short_description.description: Short description of the task (required, must contain at least one non-whitespace character)

assigned_to.description: Assigned user name in format 'first_name last_name' - must exist in database (optional)

assignment_group.description: Assignment group name - must exist in database (optional)

hr_service.description: HR service name - must exist in database (optional)

active.description: Whether task is active and available. Defaults to true.

parent_case.description: Parent case ID - must exist in database (optional)

name: create_knowledge_article
description:
Create a new knowledge article in the system.
        
        Use this tool to add a new knowledge article. The system automatically generates kb_number 
        (KB-001, KB-002, etc.) if not provided. KB numbers are unique within an organization.
        
        Required Parameters:
        - title: Article title (1-120 characters)
        
        Optional Parameters:
        - body: Article body content
        - state: Article state (draft, published, retired) - defaults to published
        - visibility: Article visibility (internal, external) - defaults to internal
        - owner_id: Owner user ID (must belong to same organization)
        
        Auto-Generated Fields:
        - kb_number: KB number (KB-001, KB-002, etc.) if not provided
        - knowledge_id: Auto-incremented ID
        - created_at and updated_at timestamps
        
        Returns the newly created knowledge article object with all fields.

owner_id.description: Owner user ID (must belong to same organization)

name: create_new_hr_case
description: Create a new HR case with complete validation. Validates that all referenced entities (hr_service, profiles, users, groups, criteria) exist in the database. Automatically generates a unique case number in format HRC#######. Returns the created case with all relationships fully expanded. Use this to initiate new HR service requests, incidents, or support cases.

status.description: Initial case status. Defaults to 'draft' if not provided.

hr_service.description: HR service ID this case relates to (must exist in database). Example: '5'. Optional.

opened_for.description: User name in format 'first_name last_name' for person case is opened for. Optional.

priority.description: Case priority. Defaults to 'planning' if not provided.

source.description: How the case was created. Optional.

assigned_to.description: User name in format 'first_name last_name'

short_description.description: Brief description of the case (required, max 120 characters). Example: 'Payroll correction needed for employee'

worknotes.description: Work notes for the case (max 120 characters). Optional.

skills.description: Array of skill IDs required for the case. Example: [1, 2, 3]. Optional.

approval_criteria.description: HR criteria ID for approval rules (must exist). Example: '2'. Optional.

approver.description: User name in format 'first_name last_name' for the approver. Optional.

account_number.description: Account number for payroll-related cases (optional, max 120 characters). Typically used for direct deposit setup or bank account changes. Example: '123456789'

name: create_new_hr_service
description: Create a new HR service with complete validation. Validates that service name is unique, fulfillment type is valid, and all referenced entities (topic detail, service template, HR criteria) exist in the database. Returns the created service with all relationships fully expanded. Use this to add new service offerings to the HR service catalog.

service_name.description: Unique service name (e.g., 'Leave of Absence Request', 'Equipment Request'). Must be unique across all services.

fulfillment_type.description: How the service request is fulfilled

topic_detail.description: Topic detail name (must exist in database). Example: 'Leave Management', 'New Employee Setup'. Optional.

service_template.description: Service template name (must exist in database). Example: 'Leave Request Template', 'Onboarding Template'. Optional.

hr_criteria.description: HR criteria name for visibility/approval (must exist in database). Example: 'HR Team Visibility', 'Admin Only Visibility'. Optional.

active.description: Whether the service is active and available. Defaults to true.

name: create_new_service_template
description: Create a new service template with validation. Validates that name is unique within organization, coe_type is valid, and change_request_values contains required fields. Returns the created template with all fields.

name.description: Service template name (must be unique within organization)

change_request_values.description: JSON object with change request default values

short_description.description: Short description for the change request

active.description: Whether template is active (default: true)

name: create_survey
description: Create a new survey with validation. At least one question must be provided. Returns the created survey with all fields and the assigned survey ID.

name: create_survey_instance
description: Create a new survey instance with validation. Assigns a user to complete a survey, optionally linking it to a case task. Can include answers to survey questions or leave them blank for later completion.

survey_id.description: ID of the survey this instance is for (required)

case_task_id.description: ID of the associated case task (optional)

assigned_to.description: ID of the user assigned to complete this survey (optional)

name: delete_hr_service
description: Soft delete an HR service by setting its active status to False. Can be identified by either hr_service_id or service_name (or both if they match). If both provided, validates they reference the same service. Validates the service exists and is currently active before deletion. Returns the deactivated service with all relationships fully expanded. Use this to remove services from active catalog while preserving data for audit trail.

hr_service_id.description: ID of the HR service to delete. Example: '1'. Provide either hr_service_id or service_name (or both if they match).

service_name.description: Name of the HR service to delete. Example: 'Old Service'. Provide either hr_service_id or service_name (or both if they match).

name: delete_notifications
description:
Delete notifications with optional filters, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Deletes notifications matching all provided filters (AND logic).
        
        Required filters (at least one):
        - notification_id: Exact match on notification ID (unique identifier)
        - hr_case_id: Exact match on HR case ID
        - email: Exact match on email address
        - type: Exact match on notification type. Valid types: report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        - status: Exact match on notification status. Valid statuses: draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        - sys_created_on: Exact match on created date/time (ISO 8601 format)
        - created_before: Filter notifications created before date (ISO 8601 format)
        - created_after: Filter notifications created after date (ISO 8601 format)
        
        Returns the number of notifications deleted.
        If no notifications match the filters, returns an error.
        
        Example:
        {
            "notification_id": 1
        }
        
        or
        
        {
            "hr_case_id": 1,
            "status": "cancelled"
        }

notification_id.description: Filter by notification ID (exact match, unique identifier)

hr_case_id.description: Filter by HR case ID (exact match)

type.description: Filter by notification type (report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other)

status.description: Filter by notification status (draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled)

sys_created_on.description: Filter by created date/time (ISO 8601 format, exact match)

created_before.description: Filter notifications created before date (ISO 8601 format)

created_after.description: Filter notifications created after date (ISO 8601 format)

name: fetch_hr_profile_by_number
description: Get a single HR profile by its profile number (e.g., HR-001, HR-042). Returns complete profile details including employment dates, manager, and all attributes.

name: fetch_hr_profiles
description: Search/list HR profiles with flexible filtering. All filters are optional and combined with AND logic. Returns list of matching profiles. Useful for finding employees by department, role, status, manager, etc.

type.description: Filter by employment type. Example: find all contractors

dob.description: Filter by date of birth (ISO format: YYYY-MM-DD)

employment_start_date.description: Filter by employment start date (ISO format: YYYY-MM-DD)

employment_end_date.description: Filter by employment end date (ISO format: YYYY-MM-DD). Use 'null' to find active employees only

manager.description: Filter by manager's hr_profile_id. Example: find all employees under manager 1

position.description: Filter by job position. Example: find all Software Engineers

name: find_group_by_name
description: Find a group by exact name (case-sensitive). Returns the group if found in the organization. Name must match exactly including case.

name.description: Group name to search for (exact match, case-sensitive). Only letters, spaces, hyphens (-), apostrophes ('), and periods (.) allowed. Example: 'IT Support' will NOT match 'it support'

name: find_hr_case_by_number
description: Get complete HR case details by unique case number. Returns full case information including all related entities (HR service, profiles, user assignments, approval criteria). Use this to retrieve comprehensive case details for review, update, or reference.

number.description: The unique case number to retrieve. Must match exactly the number column value in format HRC####### where ####### is a zero-padded 7-digit number. Examples: 'HRC0000001', 'HRC0000002', 'HRC0000770'

name: find_hr_case_knowledge_links
description:
Find HR case knowledge links with optional filters, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Use this tool to retrieve links between HR cases and knowledge articles. Without filters, 
        returns all links in the organization. With filters, returns only links matching the criteria.
        
        Optional Filters:
        - hr_case_kb_id: Filter by link ID (exact match)
        - hr_case_id: Filter by HR case ID (exact match)
        - knowledge_id: Filter by knowledge ID (exact match)
        - used_as: Filter by usage type (suggested, applied, resolution)
        
        Returns a list of link objects matching the filters, or all links if no filters provided.

hr_case_id.description: Filter by HR case ID (exact match)

knowledge_id.description: Filter by knowledge ID (exact match)

name: find_hr_services
description: Flexible search for HR services - at least ONE parameter must be provided. Search by ID, fulfillment type, topic, template, criteria, or active status. Returns matching services with all related entities (topic details, service templates, HR criteria) fully expanded.

topic_detail.description: Filter by topic detail name - partial match, case-insensitive (optional)

service_template.description: Filter by service template name - partial match, case-insensitive (optional)

hr_criteria.description: Filter by HR criteria name - partial match, case-insensitive (optional)

active.description: Filter by active status (optional)

name: find_my_cases_to_approve
description: Find all HR cases awaiting approval by a specific user. Returns cases where the user is listed as approver and request_status is 'requested'. Use this to get a user's approval queue or pending approvals workload. The Cases are returned based on the user token

name: find_notifications
description:
Find notifications with optional filters, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns a list of notifications matching all provided filters (AND logic).
        
        Optional filters:
        - notification_id: Exact match on notification ID
        - hr_case_id: Exact match on HR case ID
        - email: Exact match on email address
        - type: Exact match on notification type. Valid types: report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        - status: Exact match on notification status. Valid statuses: draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        - sys_created_on: Exact match on created date/time (ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-01-15' or '2024-01-15T09:00:00')
        
        All notifications are scoped to the user's organization.
        If no filters are provided, returns all notifications for the user's organization.

hr_case_id.description: Filter by HR case ID (exact match)

type.description: Filter by notification type (report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other)

status.description: Filter by notification status (draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled)

sys_created_on.description: Filter by created date/time (ISO 8601 format, exact match, e.g., '2024-01-15' or '2024-01-15T09:00:00')

name: find_notifications_for_email
description:
Find notifications for a specific email address, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns a list of notifications sent to the specified email address.
        
        Required parameter:
        - email: Email address to filter by (exact match)
        
        All notifications are scoped to the user's organization.

name: find_notifications_sent_for_incident
description:
Find notifications sent for a specific HR case, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns a list of notifications sent for the specified HR case.
        
        Required parameter:
        - hr_case_id: HR case ID to filter by (exact match)
        
        All notifications are scoped to the user's organization.

hr_case_id.description: HR case ID to filter by (required)

name: get_cases_assigned_to
description: Find all HR cases assigned to a specific group or user. Returns cases matching the assignment criteria with all related entities expanded. Provide either assignment_group, assigned_to, or both. Use this to see a group's or individual's current caseload.

assignment_group.description: Assignment group name (optional, but one parameter required, example: `IT Support`)

assigned_to.description: User name in format 'first_name last_name' (optional, but one parameter required)

name: get_count_of_case_priority_wise
description:
Get count of cases grouped by priority, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Returns an object with priority as the key and the count of cases which has that priority value as the value.
        Example: {'critical': 5, 'high': 3, 'low': 2}
        
        Optional parameter:
        - priority_list: List of priorities to filter. If provided, only those priorities are considered for output.
          Valid priorities: critical, high, moderate, low, planning (all lowercase, case-sensitive).
        
        If a priority list is given, the output will only include those priorities (with count 0 if not found).

priority_list.description: Optional list of priorities to filter (critical, high, moderate, low, planning)

name: get_hr_profile_by_id
description: Get HR profile by its primary key ID (hr_profile_id). Direct lookup by database ID. Returns complete profile details.

hr_profile_id.description: The unique hr_profile_id primary key. Example: '1', '42'

name: get_hr_profile_by_personal_email
description: Get HR profile by personal email address (case-insensitive lookup). Returns complete profile details if email exists.

personal_email.description: Personal email address to search. Case-insensitive. Example: 'john.doe@gmail.com'

name: get_hr_service_by_name

name: link_knowledge_to_hr_case
description:
Link a knowledge article to an HR case.
        
        Use this tool to associate a knowledge article with an HR case. The link specifies how 
        the knowledge article is used (suggested, applied, or as resolution).
        
        Required Parameters:
        - hr_case_id: HR case ID
        - knowledge_id: Knowledge article ID
        
        Optional Parameters:
        - used_as: Usage type (suggested, applied, resolution) - defaults to suggested

        A knowledge article can only be linked once to the same HR case.

name: list_assignment_rules
description: Search and list assignment rules with flexible filtering. At least one search parameter must be provided. Supports filtering by ID, name (partial match), skills (ANY match), country, priority, active status, user group, and users (ANY match). All filters combined with AND logic.

worknotes.description: Filter by worknotes - partial match, case-insensitive (optional)

active.description: Filter by active status (optional)

All parameters are optional - use any combination to filter results. Perfect for discovering cases, generating reports, or finding cases with specific characteristics.

hr_case_id.description: Filter by specific case ID. Example: '1'

number.description: Filter by case number (exact match). Must match exactly the number column value in format HRC####### where ####### is a zero-padded 7-digit number. Examples: 'HRC0000001', 'HRC0000002', 'HRC0000770'

All filters are optional and combined with AND logic. Note: 1) If you include yourself in the filter, it silently avoids self-offboarding. 2) Already offboarded profiles are automatically skipped - only active profiles will be offboarded.

user_id.description: Filter by user ID

dob.description: Filter by date of birth (ISO format: YYYY-MM-DD)

name: remove_knowledge_link_to_hr_case
description:
Remove knowledge link(s) from HR case(s), scoped to user's organization.
        
        Use this tool to remove links between knowledge articles and HR cases. You can remove:
        - A specific link by its ID (hr_case_kb_id)
        - A specific link by case and knowledge (hr_case_id + knowledge_id)
        - All links for a specific case (hr_case_id only)
        
        Required Parameter (one of):
        - hr_case_kb_id: Specific link ID (takes precedence)
        - hr_case_id + knowledge_id: Specific link by case and knowledge
        - hr_case_id: All links for this case
        
        Returns the number of links removed.

hr_case_kb_id.description: Specific link ID (takes precedence over other filters)

hr_case_id.description: HR case ID (required if hr_case_kb_id not provided)

knowledge_id.description: Knowledge article ID (required if hr_case_kb_id not provided and hr_case_id provided)

used_as.description: Filter by usage type (not used for deletion, kept for compatibility)

name: remove_user_skills
description: Remove a user skill assignment (hard delete) by user_skill_id. Permanently deletes the skill-user assignment. Returns deleted assignment details including skill_name and user information.

name: retrieve_knowledge_articles
description:
Retrieve knowledge articles with optional filters, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Use this tool to retrieve a list of knowledge articles. Without filters, returns all articles in the organization.
        With filters, returns only articles matching the specified criteria.
        
        Optional Filters:
        - knowledge_id: Filter by knowledge ID (exact match)
        - kb_number: Filter by KB number (exact match)
        - title: Filter by title (partial match, case-insensitive)
        - body: Filter by body content (partial match, case-insensitive)
        - state: Filter by state (draft, published, retired)
        - visibility: Filter by visibility (internal, external)
        - owner_id: Filter by owner user ID
        - created_before: Filter articles created before date (ISO 8601 format: 2024-01-15 or 2024-01-15T09:00:00)
        - created_after: Filter articles created after date (ISO 8601 format)
        
        Returns a list of knowledge article objects matching the filters, or all articles if no filters provided.

knowledge_id.description: Filter by knowledge ID (exact match)

body.description: Filter by body content (partial match, case-insensitive)

created_before.description: Filter articles created before this date (ISO 8601 format)

created_after.description: Filter articles created after this date (ISO 8601 format)

name: send_notification
description:
Send a new notification, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Creates a new notification for the specified HR case and email address.
        
        Required parameters:
        - hr_case_id: HR case ID (must belong to user's organization)
        - email: Recipient email address (must belong to a user in the same organization)
        
        Optional parameters:
        - type: Notification type. Valid types: report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other (default: other). All lowercase, case-sensitive.
        - status: Notification status. Valid statuses: draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled. All lowercase, case-sensitive.
        
        Example payload:
        {
            "hr_case_id": 1,
            "email": "user@example.com",
            "type": "alert",
            "status": "ready"
        }

type.description: Notification type (report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other). Default: other

status.description: Notification status (draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled)

name: update_assignment_rules

source.description: New source. Optional - only provide if changing.

assigned_to.description: User name in format 'first_name last_name' (must exist). Optional - only provide if changing.

short_description.description: New short description (max 120 characters). Optional - only provide if changing.

worknotes.description: New work notes (max 120 characters). Optional - only provide if changing.

created_after.description: For batch updates: update cases created after this date (ISO format). Example: '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'

Validates that referenced entities exist and belong to the organization. The task must belong to the authenticated user's organization. Updates only the fields provided and automatically sets the updated_at timestamp. If updating short_description, it must contain at least one non-whitespace character. name: update_hr_service
description: Update an existing HR service with smart change detection. Validates all field changes and prevents unnecessary updates by detecting if fields are already set to the provided values. Updates only the fields provided and automatically sets the updated_at timestamp. Returns the updated service with all relationships fully expanded.

hr_service_id.description: ID of the HR service to update (must exist in database). Example: 1

service_name.description: New service name (any string, must be unique). Optional - only provide if changing.

fulfillment_type.description: New fulfillment type. Optional - only provide if changing.

topic_detail.description: New topic detail name (must exist in database). Optional - only provide if changing. Example: 'Health Insurance'

service_template.description: New service template name (must exist in database). Optional - only provide if changing. Example: 'Benefits Template'

hr_criteria.description: New HR criteria name (must exist in database). Optional - only provide if changing. Example: 'Manager Approval Required'

active.description: New active status. Optional - only provide if changing.

name: update_knowledge_article
description:
Update specific fields of an existing knowledge article.
        
        Use this tool to update one or more fields of a knowledge article identified by knowledge_id or kb_number.
        At least one field (besides identifiers) must be provided. The tool validates that the new values 
        are different from current values (idempotency check).
        
        Required Parameter (one of):
        - knowledge_id: Knowledge article ID
        - kb_number: KB number
        
        Optional Parameters (at least one required):
        - title: Updated article title (1-120 characters)
        - body: Updated article body content
        - state: Updated article state (draft, published, retired)
        - visibility: Updated article visibility (internal, external)
        - owner_id: Updated owner user ID (must belong to same organization)
        
        Note: Updating a field to its current value will result in an error (no changes detected).
        
        Returns the updated knowledge article object with all fields.

knowledge_id.description: Knowledge article ID (alternative to kb_number)

owner_id.description: Updated owner user ID (must belong to same organization)

name: update_notification
description:
Update an existing notification, scoped to user's organization.
        
        Updates one or more fields of an existing notification.
        
        Required parameter:
        - notification_id: Notification ID to update
        
        Optional parameters (at least one required):
        - hr_case_id: Updated HR case ID (must belong to user's organization)
        - email: Updated recipient email address
        - type: Updated notification type. Valid types: report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        - status: Updated notification status. Valid statuses: draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled (all lowercase, case-sensitive)
        
        Example payload:
        {
            "notification_id": 1,
            "status": "ready",
            "type": "alert"
        }

type.description: Updated notification type (report, update, alert, reminder, solution_proposal, other)

status.description: Updated notification status (draft, ready, awaiting_approval, work_in_progress, closed_complete, closed_incomplete, awaiting_acceptance, suspended, cancelled)

name: update_service_template
description: Update an existing service template with smart change detection. At least one field must be provided to update. Validates name uniqueness, coe_type validity, and returns list of changes made.

service_template_id.description: ID of service template to update (required)

name.description: New service template name (optional, must be unique if changed)

short_description.description: Short description for the change request

active.description: New active status (optional)

name: update_skill
description: Update an existing skill by skill_id. At least ONE field (name or active) must be provided for update. Smart change detection - only updates changed fields. Name must be unique within organization if changed. Returns updated skill with list of changes made.

name.description: New skill name (optional, must be unique if changed)

active.description: New active status (optional)

name: update_survey
description: Update an existing survey with smart change detection. Only provides questions you want to modify; others will remain unchanged. Returns the updated survey with all fields and a list of which fields were changed.

survey_id.description: ID of the survey to update (required)

question_1.description: New question 1 text (optional, provide only if changing)

question_2.description: New question 2 text (optional, provide only if changing)

question_3.description: New question 3 text (optional, provide only if changing)

question_4.description: New question 4 text (optional, provide only if changing)

question_5.description: New question 5 text (optional, provide only if changing)

name: update_survey_instance
description: Update an existing survey instance with smart change detection. Can update assignment, associated case task, or survey responses. Only updates fields that are explicitly provided.

survey_instance_id.description: ID of the survey instance to update (required)

survey_id.description: New ID of the survey this instance is for (optional)

case_task_id.description: New ID of the associated case task (optional)

assigned_to.description: New ID of the user assigned to complete this survey (optional)

name: update_topic_category
description: Update an existing topic category with smart change detection. Only updates fields that have changed. Validates topic_category_id exists, name is unique if changed, and coe_type is valid if changed. Returns updated topic category with list of changes made.

topic_category_id.description: Topic category ID to update (required). Example: '1'

name.description: New topic category name (optional, must be unique if changed). Example: 'Updated Category Name'

coe_type.description: New COE type (optional, must be valid). Valid values: HRIT, Payroll, Talent Management, Total Rewards, Workforce Administration

active.description: New active status (optional). Example: false

name: update_topic_detail
description: Update an existing topic detail with smart change detection. Only updates fields that have changed. Validates topic_detail_id exists, name is unique if changed, and topic_category exists if provided. Returns updated topic detail with list of changes made.

topic_detail_id.description: Topic detail ID to update (required). Example: '1'

name.description: New topic detail name (optional, must be unique if changed). Example: 'Updated Topic Name'

active.description: New active status (optional). Example: false

topic_category.description: New topic category name (optional, must exist). Example: 'Onboarding'

name: update_user_details
description: Update an existing user in the HR system with smart change detection. Only updates fields that have actually changed. Validates email uniqueness, name combination uniqueness, and role validity. User must exist in organization. Returns updated user details and list of changes made.

user_id.description: ID of the user to update (required). Must exist in the organization. Example: '1', '42'

email.description: New email address (optional). Must be valid RFC-compliant email format and unique within organization. Invalid characters like *&^%#$ in email addresses are not allowed. Only provide if changing. Example: 'new.email@company.com'

first_name.description: New first name (optional, 1-60 characters). Only letters, spaces, hyphens (-), apostrophes ('), and periods (.) allowed. Special characters like @#$%^&*() are not allowed. Only provide if changing. Example: 'NewFirstName', 'Mary-Jane'

last_name.description: New last name (optional, 1-60 characters). Only letters, spaces, hyphens (-), apostrophes ('), and periods (.) allowed. Special characters like @#$%^&*() are not allowed. Only provide if changing. Example: 'NewLastName', 'O'Brien'

phone.description: New phone number (optional, max 30 characters). Only provide if changing. Example: '+1-555-999-8888'

role.description: New role (optional). Only provide if changing. Valid values determine user permissions.

active.description: New active status (optional). Set to false to deactivate user. Only provide if changing.

name: update_user_group
description: Update an existing user group with smart change detection. Only updates fields that have actually changed. Validates name uniqueness and type validity. Group must exist in organization. Returns updated group details and list of changes made.

group_id.description: ID of the group to update (required). Must exist in the organization. Example: '1', '42'

name.description: New group name (optional). Must be unique within organization. Only letters, spaces, hyphens (-), apostrophes ('), and periods (.) allowed. Special characters like @#$%^&*()!~` are not permitted. Only provide if changing. Example: 'Updated IT Support'

type.description: New group type (optional). Only provide if changing.

active.description: New active status (optional). Set to false to deactivate group. Only provide if changing.

name: add_child_incident
description:
Add a child incident to a parent incident.
        
        Use this tool to create a parent-child relationship between two incidents.
        
        Parameters:
          - parent_incident (required): Parent incident ID
          - child_incident (required): Child incident ID
        
        Returns the child incident mapping object that was created.

name: add_child_incidents
description:
Add multiple child incidents to a parent incident.
        
        Use this tool to create parent-child relationships between a parent incident and multiple child incidents.
        
        Parameters:
          - parent_incident (required): Parent incident ID
          - child_incidents (required): Array of child incident IDs
        
        Returns a list of child incident mapping objects that were created.

name: add_location
description:
Create a new location in the system.
        
        Use this tool to add a new location with the specified details. The system automatically generates
        location_id (incremental: LOC_001, LOC_002, etc.) and timestamps.
        
        Required Parameters:
          - name: Location name (must be unique)
          - city: City name (cannot be empty)
          - country: Country (cannot be empty)
        
        Optional Parameters:
          - active: Whether the location is active (default: true)
          - plot_no: Plot/building number
          - street: Street address
          - state: State/province/region
        
        Auto-Generated Fields:
          - location_id: Incremental ID (LOC_001, LOC_002, etc.)
          - created_on and updated_on timestamps
        
        Returns the newly created location object with all fields.

name.description: Location name (must be unique)

active.description: Whether the location is active

name: add_new_group_member
description: Add a new group member to a user group. Validates that group and user exist, and that the user is not already a member. Returns the newly created membership object. Requires x-itsm-user-token for authentication requirements. Returns 401 Unauthorized if token is invalid or missing. Response includes sys_* audit fields.

user_id.description: User's unique identifier

name: add_new_service
description: Add a new service to the system. Service name must be unique. Returns the newly created service object.

name.description: Service name

name: add_new_sla_definition
description:
Create a new SLA definition.

Automatically generates:
- sla_def_id (SLA_001, SLA_002, ...)

Required fields:
- name: Unique name for the SLA definition (<=120 chars)
- metric: response or resolution
- target_mins: Target time in minutes (>=1)
- pause_on_pending: Boolean indicating if SLA pauses on pending status
- active: Boolean indicating if the SLA definition is active

Optional fields:
- applies_to_priority: CRITICAL, HIGH, MODERATE, LOW
- schedule: Schedule ID

Example payload:
{
    "name": "Critical Response SLA",
    "metric": "RESPONSE",
    "target_mins": 60,
    "pause_on_pending": true,
    "active": true,
    "applies_to_priority": "CRITICAL"
}

name.description: Name of the SLA definition (unique, <=120 chars)

pause_on_pending.description: Whether to pause SLA on pending status

active.description: Whether the SLA definition is active

name: add_new_user
description:
Create a new user in the system.
        
        Use this tool to add a new user with the specified details. The system automatically generates
        user_id (incremental: USER_001, USER_002, etc.), user_name (from first.last), and other system fields.
        
        Authentication Requirements:
          - x-itsm-user-token: Optional user authentication token. Validates the requester's identity.
          - API returns 401 Unauthorized if provided token is invalid.
        
        Required Parameters:
          - first_name: User's first name (1-60 characters)
          - last_name: User's last name (1-60 characters)
          - email: User's email address (must be unique and valid format)
          - phone: User's phone number (format: +1-415-555-0101, must be unique)
          - role: User's role (must be one of: admin, manager, agent, reporter)
          - active: Whether the user account is active (true or false)
        
        Optional Parameters:
          - user_name: User login name (generated from first.last if not provided)
          - location_id: Location identifier
        
        Note: The organization ID (org_id) is automatically set from the authenticated user's organization.
        
        Auto-Generated Fields:
          - user_id: Incremental ID (USER_001, USER_002, etc.)
          - user_name: Generated from first_name.last_name (lowercase)
          - static_token: Secure authentication token
          - created_on and updated_on timestamps
          - sys_id and other audit fields
        
        Returns the newly created user object with all fields.

email.description: User's email address (valid email format required)

active.description: Whether the user account is active

user_name.description: User login name (generated from first.last if not provided)

name: add_new_user_group
description: Add a new user group to the system. Group name must be unique. Returns the newly created group object. Requires x-itsm-user-token for authentication requirements. Returns 401 Unauthorized if token is invalid or missing. Response includes sys_* audit fields.

name.description: Group's name

active.description: Whether the group is active

Calculate the average number of notifications per incident.

Compute the average of target minutes grouped by priority.

name: count_incident_for_assignment_group

Count incidents for a specific assignment group with optional filters.

Count notifications grouped by status.

Count notifications grouped by type.

name: create_change
description:
Create a new change request.

Automatically generates:
- change_id (CHG_001, CHG_002, ...)
- number (CHG0000001, CHG0000002, ...)

Required fields:
- short_description: Brief description (<=120 chars)
- status: Change status (new, assess, authorize, scheduled, implement, review, closed, canceled)
- impact: Impact level (high, medium, low)
- risk: Risk level (high, medium, low)
- priority: Priority level (critical, high, moderate, low)

Optional fields:
- service: Service ID
- service_offering: Service offering ID
- configuration_item: Configuration item ID
- category: Change category (network, software, hardware, documentation, system_software, application_software, service, telecom, other)
- description: Detailed description (<=120 chars)
- implementation_plan: Implementation plan (<=120 chars)
- testing_plan: Testing plan (<=120 chars)
- cab_required: Boolean indicating if CAB approval is needed
- assigned_to: Assigned user ID
- assignment_group: Assigned group ID
- close_code: Close code (successful, successful_with_issues, unsuccessful)
- close_notes: Close notes (<=120 chars)

Example payload:
{
    "short_description": "Upgrade database cluster",
    "status": "assess",
    "impact": "high",
    "risk": "high",
    "priority": "critical",
    "category": "service",
    "implementation_plan": "Rollover to replica, upgrade primary, fail back"
}

status.description: Change status (new, assess, authorize, scheduled, implement, review, closed, canceled)

priority.description: Priority level (critical, high, moderate, low)

category.description: Change category (network, software, hardware, documentation, system_software, application_software, service, telecom, other)

assigned_to.description: Assigned user ID

name: create_incident
description:
Create a new incident in the system.
        
        Use this tool to create a new incident with the specified details.
        
        Required Parameters:
          - short_description: Brief description of the incident
          - caller_id: ID of the user who reported the incident
        
        Optional Parameters (all can be null/omitted):
          - service: Service ID related to the incident
          - service_offering: Service offering ID related to the incident
          - configuration_item: Configuration item ID related to the incident
          - channel: How the incident was reported (self-service, phone, email, chat, walk-in, virtual-agent)
          - status: Current status of the incident (new, in_progress, on_hold, resolved, closed, canceled). Default: "new"
          - category: Category of the incident (inquiry-help, software, hardware, database, password-reset, network). Default: "inquiry-help"
          - description: Detailed description of the incident
          - impact: Impact level (high, medium, low). Default: "low"
          - urgency: Urgency level (high, medium, low). Default: "low"
          - priority: Priority level (critical, high, moderate, low, planning). Default: "planning"
          - assigned_to: User ID to assign the incident to
          - assignment_group: Group ID to assign the incident to
          - worknotes: Work notes for the incident
          - resolution_notes: Resolution notes for the incident
          - close_notes: Close notes for the incident
          - resolution_code: Resolution code for the incident
          - parent_incident: Parent incident ID if this is a child incident
          - problem: Problem ID related to the incident
          - change_request: Change request ID related to the incident
          - caused_by_change: Change ID that caused this incident
          - resolved_by: User ID who resolved the incident
          - on_hold_reason: Reason why the incident is on hold
          - incident_template: Incident template ID to use
          - resolved: Timestamp when the incident was resolved
        
        Default Values:
          When a parameter is null or omitted, the following defaults are applied:
          - status: "new"
          - category: "inquiry-help"
          - impact: "low"
          - urgency: "low"
          - priority: "planning"
        
        Auto-Generated Fields:
          - incident_id: Unique identifier for the incident (format: INC_001, INC_002, etc.)
          - number: Incident number (e.g., INC-000001)
          - created_at: Timestamp when the incident was created
          - updated_at: Timestamp when the incident was last updated
        
        Returns the newly created incident object with all fields.

service.description: Service ID related to the incident

service_offering.description: Service offering ID related to the incident

configuration_item.description: Configuration item ID related to the incident

caller_id.description: ID of the user who reported the incident

channel.description: How the incident was reported (self-service, phone, email, chat, walk-in, virtual-agent)

status.description: Current status of the incident. Default: 'new' if null or omitted

category.description: Category of the incident. Default: 'inquiry-help' if null or omitted

impact.description: Impact level. Default: 'low' if null or omitted

urgency.description: Urgency level. Default: 'low' if null or omitted

priority.description: Priority level. Default: 'planning' if null or omitted

assigned_to.description: User ID to assign the incident to

assignment_group.description: Group ID to assign the incident to

parent_incident.description: Parent incident ID if this is a child incident

problem.description: Problem ID related to the incident

change_request.description: Change request ID related to the incident

caused_by_change.description: Change ID that caused this incident

resolved_by.description: User ID who resolved the incident

on_hold_reason.description: Reason why the incident is on hold

resolved.description: Timestamp when the incident was resolved (ISO 8601 format)

Create a new knowledge article in the system.

        generates knowledge_id (KB_001, KB_002, etc.), kb_number (KB0000001, KB0000002, etc.), and timestamps.
        Returns the newly created knowledge article object with all fields.

name: create_new_incident_template
description:
Create a new incident template in the system.
        
        Use this tool to add a new incident template with the specified details. The system automatically
        generates incident_template_id (incremental: TMPL_001, TMPL_002, etc.) and timestamps.
        
        Required Parameters:
          - name: Template name (1-120 characters, must be unique)
          - change_request_values: JSON object containing template fields
        
        Required fields inside change_request_values:
          - caller_id: User ID who is the default caller
          - short_description: Brief description (1-120 characters)
        
        Optional fields inside change_request_values:
          - channel: Incident channel (values: SELF_SERVICE, PHONE, EMAIL, CHAT, WALK_IN, VIRTUAL_AGENT)
          - category: Incident category (values: INQUIRY_HELP, SOFTWARE, HARDWARE, DATABASE, PASSWORD_RESET)
          - impact: Impact level (values: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) - defaults to LOW
          - urgency: Urgency level (values: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) - defaults to LOW
          - priority: Priority level (values: CRITICAL, HIGH, MODERATE, LOW, PLANNING) - defaults to PLANNING
          - configuration_item: Configuration item ID
          - service: Service ID
          - service_offering: Service offering ID
        
        Optional Parameters:
          - active: Whether the template is active (defaults to true)
        
        Auto-Generated Fields:
          - incident_template_id: Incremental ID (TMPL_001, TMPL_002, etc.)
          - created_at and updated_at timestamps
        
        Returns the newly created incident template object with all fields.

name.description: Template name (unique, 1-120 characters)

change_request_values.description: JSON object containing template fields. Required: caller_id, short_description. Optional: channel, category, impact, urgency, priority, configuration_item, service, service_offering

priority.description: Priority level (defaults to 'planning')

active.description: Whether the template is active (defaults to true)

name: create_problem

Create a new problem record.

Auto-generates:

name: delete_change_request_mappings
description:
Delete change request mappings using precise filters with AND logic.

This tool deletes change request mappings based on filter criteria. It requires at least one
filter and uses AND logic when multiple filters are provided (all filters must match).

Safety requirements:
- You **must** provide at least one filter (`change_request_mapping_id`, `change_id`, `incident_id`, or `problem_id`).
- If multiple filters are provided, ALL must match (AND logic) - this ensures precise deletion.
- Prevents accidental bulk deletions by requiring all specified criteria to match.

Returns:
- deleted_count: Number of mappings deleted
- deleted_mappings: List of deleted mapping objects with full details
- message: Success message indicating what was deleted

Examples:
- Delete by mapping ID: {"change_request_mapping_id": "CRM_001"}
- Delete by change and incident: {"change_id": "CHG_001", "incident_id": "INC_001"}
- Delete by change only: {"change_id": "CHG_001"}

incident_id.description: Delete mappings linked to this incident.

problem_id.description: Delete mappings linked to this problem.

Delete Incident SLA records filtered by identifiers or timestamps.

created_after.description: Created_on >= timestamp

name: find_configuration_item_by_serial_number
description:
Retrieve a configuration item by its serial number.
        
        Use this tool to find a specific CI using its serial number as the identifier.
        The serial number is unique across all configuration items.
        
        Parameters:
          - serial_number (required): Configuration item serial number
        
        Returns a single configuration item object if found, or an error if the CI doesn't exist.

name: find_configuration_items
description:
List configuration items with optional filters.
        
        Use this tool to retrieve a list of configuration items. Without filters, returns all CIs.
        With filters, returns only CIs matching the specified criteria.
        
        Optional Filters:
          - configuration_item_id: Filter by CI ID (exact match)
          - owner_id: Filter by owner user ID (exact match)
          - location_id: Filter by location ID (exact match)
          - serial_number: Filter by serial number (exact match)
          - status: Filter by status (IN_USE, IN_STOCK, MAINTENANCE, RETIRED, DISPOSED)
          - cost: Filter by cost (exact match)
          - created_after: Filter CIs created after date (ISO 8601 format: 2024-01-15 or 2024-01-15T09:00:00)
          - created_before: Filter CIs created before date (ISO 8601 format)

name: cancel_virtual_event_townhall
description:
Cancel a virtualEventTownhall. A canceled town hall has its status set to canceled permanently.
        
        CRITICAL: Only the Organizer (creator) can cancel a townhall.
        Co-organizers CANNOT cancel.
        
        **Action:** Changes townhall status to 'canceled' permanently
        
        **Status Transitions:**
        - draft → canceled (allowed, returns 204 No Content)
        - published → canceled (allowed, returns 204 No Content)
        - canceled → canceled (idempotent, returns 200 OK with message)
        
        **Permissions Required:**
        - VirtualEvent.ReadWrite:delegated (only delegated, NOT application)
        
        **Response:** 204 No Content on success (no response body)
        
        **Authorization:**
        - ONLY the Organizer can cancel
        - Co-organizers are NOT allowed to cancel
        - Non-organizers will receive 403 Forbidden
        
        **Note:** You can still get a canceled town hall by using the Get virtualEventTownhall API.
        
        **API Endpoint:** POST /solutions/virtualEvents/townhalls/{townhallId}/cancel
        
        Permissions (EXACT from Microsoft Documentation):
        - Delegated (work or school account): VirtualEvent.ReadWrite (least privileged)
        - Delegated (personal Microsoft account): NOT SUPPORTED
        - Application: NOT SUPPORTED
        
        Request Parameters:
        - townhall_id (required): The unique identifier of the townhall (format: guid@guid)
        
        Response:
        - 204 No Content: Townhall successfully canceled
        - 200 OK: Townhall already canceled (idempotent)
        - 404 Not Found: Townhall doesn't exist
        - 403 Forbidden: User is not the organizer
        
        Important Notes:
        - No request body required
        - Only the organizer (creator) can cancel
        - Co-organizers cannot cancel (same restriction as publish)
        - Can cancel from any status (draft or published)
        - Idempotent: Canceling already canceled townhall returns 200 OK
        - Canceled townhalls remain accessible via GET API
        
        Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/virtualeventtownhall-cancel

name: create_audio_routing_group
description:
Create a new audio routing group for a call.

The audio routing group stores a private audio route between participants in a
multiparty conversation. Source is the participant itself and the receivers are
a subset of other participants in the multiparty conversation.

IMPORTANT NOTES:
- **PERMISSION REQUIRED**: Application-only permission (NO delegated)
  - Calls.JoinGroupCall.All (least privileged)
  - Calls.InitiateGroupCall.All (higher privileged)
- **4-speaker limit**: Only top 4 dominant speakers' audio forwarded in group calls
- If speaker not loud enough in main mixer, bot won't hear even with private audio group

ROUTING MODES:
1. **oneToOne** (1 source ↔ 1 receiver):
   - Immutable after creation (cannot be updated)
   - Exactly 1 source participant required
   - Exactly 1 receiver participant required
   - For private 1-to-1 audio channel

2. **multicast** (1 source → multiple receivers):
   - Source has 1 participant
   - Multiple receivers allowed
   - Receiver list can be updated later
   - Useful for broadcast scenarios

CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES (Per Microsoft Graph API):
- Sources must have exactly 1 participant ID (the authenticated bot/application)
- Source participant MUST be the authenticated bot making the API call
- Receivers must have at least 1 participant ID
- Routing mode MUST match participant count:
  * 1 source + 1 receiver → MUST use "oneToOne" mode
  * 1 source + 2+ receivers → MUST use "multicast" mode
- Parent call must be in active state (not terminated/terminating)
- All participants must exist in the call and belong to same organization

Permissions (Application only):
- Calls.JoinGroupCall.All (least privileged)
- Calls.InitiateGroupCall.All (higher privileged)

Note: Delegated permissions are NOT supported.

routingMode.description: Routing mode: oneToOne (immutable) or multicast (updatable receivers)

sources.description: Source participant IDs (must have exactly 1 participant - the authenticated bot/application making this API call)

receivers.description: Receiver participant IDs. For oneToOne mode: exactly 1 receiver. For multicast mode: 2 or more receivers.

          - surname: Surname/last name (max 128 characters)
          - jobTitle: Job title (max 128 characters)
          - mail: Primary email address (max 320 characters)
          - businessPhones: Array of business phone numbers
          - mobilePhone: Mobile phone number
          - officeLocation: Office location (max 128 characters)

        Response Structure:
          - Returns created user with Microsoft Graph API v1.0 format:
            * @odata.context: Metadata context URL

          - 409: Conflict - User with same userPrincipalName already exists

name: create_virtual_event_townhall
description:
Create a new virtualEventTownhall object in draft mode.

        API Endpoint: POST /solutions/virtualEvents/townhalls

        Permissions (EXACT from Microsoft Documentation):
        - Delegated (work or school account): VirtualEvent.ReadWrite (least privileged)
        - Delegated (personal Microsoft account): NOT SUPPORTED
        - Application: NOT SUPPORTED

        CRITICAL: Only delegated permissions with work/school account are supported.

        CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: The isInviteOnly property can ONLY be true if the audience property is set to 'organization'.

        Request Body Properties (all following Microsoft Graph API v1.0 spec):
        - displayName (required): The display name of the townhall (1-500 characters)
        - description (required): A description with:
          - contentType: 'text' or 'html'
          - content: The description text
        - startDateTime (required): Start date-time with:
          - dateTime: ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2024-03-30T10:00:00')
          - timeZone: Timezone name (e.g., 'Pacific Standard Time')
        - endDateTime (required): End date-time (must be after startDateTime) with:
          - dateTime: ISO 8601 format
          - timeZone: Timezone name
        - audience (required): Townhall visibility
          - Possible values: 'everyone', 'organization', 'unknownFutureValue'
        - isInviteOnly (optional): Whether townhall is invite-only (default: false)
          - Can ONLY be true if audience='organization'
        - invitedAttendees (optional): Array of user/guest identities, each with:
          - id: User/Guest ID (required)
          - email: Email for guest identities (optional, if provided identifies as guest)
          - displayName: Display name (optional, auto-populated for users)
        - coOrganizers (optional): Array of user identities, each with:
          - id: User ID (required)
          - tenantId: Tenant ID (required) - displayName auto-populated from database
        - settings (optional): Townhall settings with:
          - isAttendeeEmailNotificationEnabled: Boolean (default: false)

        Response Properties:
        - id: Unique identifier (format: guid@guid)
        - status: Townhall status (always 'draft' on creation)
        - displayName, description, startDateTime, endDateTime, audience: From request
        - isInviteOnly: From request (default: false)
        - invitedAttendees: Array of invited user/guest identities (with details populated)
        - createdBy: Creator identity information (auto-populated from authenticated user)
          - application: null
          - device: null
          - user: User identity with @odata.type, id, displayName, tenantId
        - coOrganizers: Array of coorganizer identities (with displayName populated)
        - settings: Townhall settings
        - externalEventInformation: Empty array initially

        Important Notes:
        - Townhalls are always created in 'draft' status
        - Only delegated permissions supported (no application permissions)
        - Personal Microsoft accounts are NOT supported
        - endDateTime must be after startDateTime
        - isInviteOnly can ONLY be true if audience='organization'
        - CoOrganizers must exist in the system
        - Invited attendees can be users (must exist) or guests (validated by email)
        - Creator information is auto-populated from authenticated user

        Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/virtualeventsroot-post-townhalls
